title: Manisha Bhanwala's Comeback Gold Caps India's Best-Ever Women's Wrestling Worlds
excerpt: Trailing 0-6 in the 59kg final in Astana, Bhanwala beat American Abigail Nette 8-6 to become India's first woman senior world champion, as the team finished with four medals.
body:
• Manisha Bhanwala defeated the United States' Abigail Nette 8-6 in the women's 59kg final in Astana on October 30, recovering from 0-6 down, to become India's first woman to win a senior World Wrestling Championships gold.
  • She is only the second Indian wrestler to win a senior world title, after Sushil Kumar in 2010.
  • India finished with four medals — Bhanwala's gold, silvers for Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg), and bronze for Tanu Sharma (72kg) — its best-ever haul in women's wrestling, surpassing the two-medal returns of 2012 and 2021.
  • India placed fourth in the medal standings and fifth in the team rankings with 94 points, behind the United States, Japan, China and Ukraine.

It took three finals in three days, but India finally has a women's world wrestling champion. Manisha Bhanwala, 29, defeated Abigail Nette of the United States 8-6 in the 59kg final at the World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, on Friday, fighting back from 0-6 down to win a bout that had looked lost, IANS reported.

The gold makes Bhanwala the first Indian woman to win a senior World Championships title and only the second Indian wrestler to do so, after Sushil Kumar's men's 66kg title in 2010. It also closed a landmark week: Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg) had reached finals earlier in the competition and taken silver — the hurdle Anshu Malik had fallen at in 2021 — before Bhanwala crossed it. Tanu Sharma's bronze in the 72kg class completed a four-medal haul.

"Records are meant to be broken, and I want this record and achievement to be broken as well. I want more and more girls to emerge as world champions so that Indian women wrestlers winning world titles becomes the norm rather than an exception."

— Manisha Bhanwala, speaking to IANS

A best-ever campaign

The four medals surpassed India's previous best women's returns at the Worlds — two medals each in 2012 and 2021 — and, for the first time in the competition's 35-year history, Indian women reached three finals at a single edition, according to The Indian Express. India finished fourth in the medal standings and fifth in the team rankings with 94 points, behind the United States, Japan, China and Ukraine. High performance director Ian Butler rated the performance "eight out of ten" to The Indian Express, saying the squad had bounced back from its Asian Games disappointment with room still to improve.

President Droupadi Murmu praised Bhanwala on Saturday, saying her achievement had brought "immense pride and glory" to the nation, IANS reported.

What comes next

Bhanwala's next task is to move down from 59kg to the Olympic 57kg category with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in view, IANS reported. Women's head coach Virender Dahiya backed Sirohi and Dhochak to build on their silvers alongside her. "We also aim to break records at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics," Bhanwala said.
